title: Redirects: Writing & Appending 📝
description: Create and extend files using > and >>. Use tee to write and display simultaneously.

slides.title: Standard Output Streams 🌊
slides.content:
## stdout and stderr

Every command has two output streams:
- `stdout` (file descriptor 1) – normal output.
- `stderr` (file descriptor 2) – error messages.

Redirects let you send these streams to files instead of the terminal.

slides.title: Overwrite with >
slides.content: `command > file` writes stdout to file, overwriting it.

quizData.question: What happens to `data.txt` when you run `echo 'new' > data.txt`?

options.text: It replaces the entire content with 'new'
It creates a second file called 'new'

quizData.explanation: A single `>` truncates the file and writes the new content.

slides.title: Append with >>
slides.content: `>>` adds output to the end of the file, preserving existing data.
slides.codeSnippet:
echo "Line 1" > log.txt
echo "Line 2" >> log.txt
cat log.txt

slides.title: Redirecting stderr 🚨
slides.content:
## Error Output to a File

- `command 2> error.log` – writes only stderr.
- `command > out.log 2>&1` – merges stderr into stdout and writes both.
- `command &> all.log` – shortcut to redirect both stdout and stderr (Bash).

quizData.question: How do you redirect both stdout and stderr to the same file in modern Bash?
quizData.explanation: `&> filename` (or `>& filename`) sends both streams to the file.

slides.title: tee: See and Save 🧪
slides.content: `tee` reads from stdin and writes to both stdout and one or more files. Perfect for logging while watching.

slides.title: ⚠️ Clobber Protection
slides.content: Set `set -o noclobber` to prevent `>` from overwriting existing files. Use `>|` to force overwrite when noclobber is on.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: Use `/dev/null` as a black hole: `command > /dev/null 2>&1` hides all output completely.
